thread:
chris: deploy-bot flagged a sustained p95 latency increase on canary for release v5.0.2. We did not auto-revert. Can someone pick this up?

deploy-bot: ALERT v5.0.2-canary: p95=980ms (6m window). Auto-revert threshold=1000ms. No auto action taken.

mina: Looks like it hovered just under auto threshold but steady. I see increased queue depth on the inference workers. Recommend manual hold of canary traffic and pin dedicated pools to v5.0.1 while we investigate.

infra-oncall: Can hold traffic via `deployctl traffic set canary 0% --slice=canary-7` and pin: `releasectl pin --pool=dedicated --version=5.0.1 --reason="temporary pin due to canary p95"`. Waiting approval.

chris: Approve both. Do NOT trigger full rollback yet. This smells like a warmup/queueing issue, not correctness. @support prepare a short customer note for dedicated customers explaining a temporary routing pin.

support: Draft: "We temporarily pinned dedicated routing to v5.0.1 while we investigate transient latency on v5.0.2 canary. No data loss; most requests unaffected. Contact support if you see persistent latency." Ready to post after infra confirms hold.

infra-oncall: Hold applied, pin succeeded. Command output: `OK - canary traffic 0% (drain), pinned dedicated to v5.0.1`.

mina: Restarted the suspect worker to force KV cache rebuild. Monitoring: p95 dropped to ~360ms. Recommend ramp to 5% over 10m and watch. Escalation rules: if p95 > 1100ms for 2 consecutive 5m windows OR error-rate >1% for 5m then run `releasectl rollback --version=5.0.1 --reason=escalation` and notify customers.

chris: Agreed. Summary: manual hold + pin applied, restart performed, ramping gradually. This thread is the single source of truth for rollback criteria and comms. I'll own follow-up postmortem if we hit escalation.

deploy-bot: ACK policy and will alert if thresholds breached."
